reasons.A: Cliff valkyrie: the run's clearest armoured gown, a pale sky-blue steel A-line with a real bell from the hip under a white bow-winged helm, one pale blue bell from the ARPG camera (second critic 7.35, first; first critic 7.13, first).
reasons.B: Storm sister: a bright cloud-white skirt of jagged wind-cut panels that flares hard under grey-blue plate and a winged helm, the most wind in any set (second critic 7.0, second; it rose from 6.33).
reasons.D: Eyrie keeper: a cloud-white bodice over a sky-blue skirt with tan leather and a steel feather-crested half-helm, the only take carrying the brief's rock tan (second critic 5.6, third).

fixes.A: Slim the full-width block sleeves and drop the shoulder caps; carry the light colours round the dark back; add wind movement and rock-tan trim.
fixes.B: The dark navy block sleeves read as pauldrons: slim and lighten them; sweep the hem shards one way, as if the wind took them.
fixes.D: The split skirt hangs straight and reads as a tabard: splay it into one A-line, and drop the wide white cuff rings.

notes: 6 of 6 survived the draft and the rework with no resume (g00 and g02 hit the 40-turn cap in the rework; both still pass). Again no set made slim sleeves; most backs are dark and vanish at night, and the palette's rock tan barely appears. The pale sky-and-cloud palette reads far better from above than any dark gown in the wave. A and B led both passes.
